class.name: NetwSessionConfig
class.brief_description: Draft the session machine is initialized from, declared on a scope node.
class.description: [method Netw.configure_session] returns a draft the scope node owns. Edit it in place or through the fluent methods, and the session copies its values once, at a deferred boundary after the declaring call stack has finished. From then on the session holds owned values and this Resource is a spent authoring snapshot: a later setter reports the late write and moves nothing. This resource carries only the facts the wire and the session machine own. What a session hosts or joins over is not among them: that is an argument of the verb that hosts, on [NetwConnectHandle]. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_session(self) \ .app_id(&"bomber-v2") \ .desired_role(NetwMultiplayer.Role.LISTEN_SERVER) [/codeblock] A preset handed to that verb is copied rather than kept, so one [code].tres[/code] may seed several scenes and editing it afterwards reaches none of them. Nested [NetwLinkConditions] and [NetwServerInfo] values are copied too. [method NetwMultiplayer.session_get_config] returns a detached snapshot of the running values, freshly copied nested objects included. Editing what it returns is a way to read the session, never a way to configure it. A [MultiplayerTree]'s session exports are the fallback when no node declares one. An explicit declaration replaces that export whole, so a field left at its default here is the default rather than the tree's value, and the discarded non-default tree fields are named once in a warning.

members.member: Game-build tag that gates session admission. A joining peer whose tag differs is rejected during authentication before it reaches [method MultiplayerAPI.get_peers]. Leave this empty to disable the check. The session derives one auth tag from this value. It also names the space a signalled transport creates its room codes in, and is what makes a code short enough to read out. See [member MultiplayerTree.app_id].

The [enum NetwMultiplayer.Role] the local peer intends to play once a session starts. The live [member NetwMultiplayer.role] is only assigned when the session reaches [constant NetwMultiplayer.SessionState.ONLINE]. This is the intent the assignment edge reads to pick the server role. A value outside the enum is rejected and the previous role stands. An embedded server is constructed with a dedicated-server role that constrains the effective role after consumption, whichever declaration supplied the other values.

Optional latency and loss simulation applied to this session's peer. [NetwMultiplayer] wraps the built peer with it before assignment, so a session applies what it was configured with whether or not a [MultiplayerTree] owns it. Its four scalar fields are copied at consumption, so mutating the object afterwards reaches no running session.

What this session tells a probing client about itself: its name, its player cap, its [enum NetwServerInfo.Visibility], and whatever else the game fills in. This is the whole advert and its only door, authored in the inspector or declared before the session is brought up. [method NetwServerInfo.from_session] copies it and overlays the fields only a live session knows, so a game that leaves it unset still returns a probe honestly and a game that sets it never says the same thing twice. Its values, nested containers included, are copied at consumption. [codeblock] var info := NetwServerInfo.new() info.motd = "Friday night" info.max_players = 8 Netw.configure_session(self).server_info(info) [/codeblock] A game that computes its reply per probe declares a provider through [method Netw.configure_server_info] instead. That provider is handed this record, already copied and filled in from the live session, and returns the reply to send.
